answer: An agent economy can make identity costly through stake-backed endorsements: each newcomer deposits collateral, and several established agents sign its access credential. If the newcomer duplicates votes or coordinates fraud, a fraud proof burns its stake and penalizes the endorsers. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund many identities and persuade honest agents to risk capital, so fake trust scales with real cost; names such as tundra, cedar, and beacon offer no shortcut.
